tender.title: Provision of an Enterprise Asset Management Package
tender.procurementMethodRationale:
GATLs existing Octave Attune EAM solution is supplied by Intergraph (UK) Limited. Its integration, web-service and data-movement capabilities support controlled exchange of relevant information with connected corporate, operational, reporting and engineering systems, including third-parties: leasing companies, manufacturers and maintainers. Loss of access would result in extreme disruption to the operation of passenger services.
Replacement by an alternative supplier would require the redevelopment and revalidation of multiple interfaces and integrations across stations, rolling stock, and operational control environments. This would involve significant cost, resource requirements, technical risk, and potential disruption to critical passenger information services.

Contingent labour provision of a technical subject matter expert relating to eIDAS, for up to 100 days per annum.
The consultant will:

• serve as the ICO's technical subject matter expert for associated standards relating to electronic signatures, qualified digital certificates, electronic seals, timestamps and other authentication mechanisms.

tender.title: Transparency Notice for extension to Cabinet Office Call Off from Independent Shared Service Centre 2 (ISSC2 Framework)
tender.description:
This notice signals the intention of the Cabinet Office to make a direct award to Shared Services Connected Limited (SSCL) to extend the Call-Off Contract held under the ISSC2 Framework for up to an additional 18 months.
The extension is required to secure the continued provision of business-critical back-office operations, including human resources, finance and accounts, payroll and procurement to maintain operational continuity while transitioning services to replacement service providers under the Matrix programme.
The direct award is justified under Schedule 5 of the Procurement Act 2023 due to technical constraints and the absence of competition for technical reasons, as an interim supplier would cause severe technical incompatibility, service disruption, and substantial duplication of costs.
tender.procurementMethodRationale:
Single supplier - technical reasons:
The back-office operations rely on the legacy Single Operating Platform (SOP). The highly complex architecture and proprietary systems managed by SSCL mean no alternative supplier can step in for an interim period without causing severe operational disruption to payroll, HR, and financial administration.
Additional or repeat goods, services or works - extension or partial replacement:
This extension provides additional continuity of identical services following the original 2013 competitive procurement, where switching to an interim supplier before the Matrix go-live would cause disproportionate technical difficulty and substantial duplication of costs.

documents.description: Not published

tender.riskDetails:
Risk of additional technical or operational delays in the full implementation, cutover, or go-live of the replacement Matrix solution beyond the target 18-month transition window, necessitating an additional short-term extension or phased tapering to ensure uninterrupted operational continuity.
Risk of unexpected complex exit dependencies, data migration bottlenecks, or technical interface failures arising between the legacy Single Operating Platform (SOP) architecture and replacement systems during parallel running, cutover, or decommissioning phases.
Risk of unexpected operational or cyber-security incidents affecting critical shared services (including civil service payroll, financial processing, and grant administration) during transition, requiring emergency adjustments to resource capacity, technical support levels, or the transition timetable.

tender.title: Procurement for a Developer for Brimscombe Port, Stroud, Gloucestershire.
tender.description:
:Stroud District Council wishes to procure a developer partner to deliver its Brimscombe Port development. Brimscombe Port was at one time the largest inland port in the Country dating back to the 1780’s. Following the decline in canals the Port became redundant. The canal was in-filled after the Second World War and the site developed as an industrial estate during the 1960/70’s. Today the industrial estate has been demolished, ready for redevelopment , the Listed Port Mill and salt warehouse add to the site's spectacular setting
SDC is leading on the delivery of the redevelopment of Brimscombe Port in conjunction with Stroud Valleys Canal Company (SVCC) and Homes England (HE), to reinstate the canal and provide a mixed use residential led development on a ten-acre site. Please see Procurement documents for further details.
